policies.title: Named EU ordinary passports: Ukraine short-visit visa waiver
policies.summary: Ukraine's live current-edition Presidential Decree waives visas for citizens of EU Member States entering or transiting Ukraine for stays not exceeding 90 days.
conditions: Applies to a citizen of the named current EU Member State travelling on that state's standard ordinary passport for a short visitor entry or transit.
The Ukrainian Decree itself establishes the named EU-Member-State class; this is not an inference from EU or Schengen rules applicable elsewhere.
The Decree states a stay may not exceed 90 days. It does not itself state an 180-day calculation, so none is asserted here.
Work, residence, diplomatic, service, emergency and other special travel documents, wartime operational access, and final admission remain outside this baseline.

policies.title: Luxembourg ordinary passports: Ukraine short-visit visa waiver with official-source conflict
policies.summary: Ukraine's current-edition Presidential Decree waives visas for Luxembourg citizens as citizens of an EU Member State, while Luxembourg's January 2026 traveller page inconsistently directs its nationals to Ukraine's e-Tourist Visa service.
conditions: The Ukrainian destination law is the controlling admission rule and the Rada portal presents it as the current edition without a lost-force marker; the current EU directory confirms Luxembourg remains in the covered class.

Luxembourg's traveller page, updated 7 January 2026, directly conflicts by directing Luxembourg nationals to obtain an e-Tourist Visa. This discrepancy is preserved and keeps the relationship at medium confidence and on an early recheck cycle.
The Decree states a stay may not exceed 90 days. It does not itself state an 180-day calculation, so none is asserted here.
Work, residence, diplomatic, service, emergency and other special travel documents, wartime operational access, and final admission remain outside this baseline.
